title: The close commit of a host project is pushed by a backlog.py command, not by hand (second-project run)
goal: A host project pushes its close commit with a backlog.py command that runs land_push (the skill names it), since close deletes the items land needs and a hand push is denied to agents

run:
import argparse, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import backlog, bl_cli
ap = bl_cli.build_parser("x", ".")
sub = next(a for a in ap._actions if isinstance(a, argparse._SubParsersAction))
text = " ".join(sub.choices["close"].format_help().split())
print("land_push" in text)
sys.exit(0 if "land_push" in text else 1)

clauses.clause: A host project pushes its close commit with a backlog.py command that runs land_push (the skill names it), since close deletes the items land needs and a hand push is denied to agents

notes: Run findings 21 and 27: the skill tells the orchestrator to push the claims with land_push's argv by hand (git push denied); land ST-... --branch main after close --commit: no item ST-...: its file was deleted (a closed sprint's item); the close commit stayed local. Planning 2026-10-24: the claim-push half is delivered by ST-44md64ps (backlog.py begin pushes the claim commits through land_push); this story keeps the close-commit half and stays parked.
